stories.title: Startup builds AI model to decipher electrical signals plants use to 'speak'
stories.summary: Electric Plant has built an AI model that attempts to translate the subtle electrical signals running through plant stems, aiming to let humans interpret what plants are 'saying.'
stories.more: The startup's AI-powered translator reads electrical activity in plant stems and tries to render it as interpretable signals for humans. Further details on the model's accuracy or methodology were not included in the Source's excerpt for this Edition.

items.title: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language
items.excerpt: Electric Plant has built an AI-powered translator to help humans listen to what plants are saying with the subtle electricity coursing through their stems.

stories.title: Spotify removed 50 million AI-generated 'slop' tracks from recommendations
stories.summary: Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million AI-generated or spam songs from its recommendations over the past year, and adjusted its recommendation system to surface more human-made music.
stories.more: Spotify announced on Tuesday that it pulled over 50 million tracks considered AI 'slop' or spam from user recommendations over the past year. The company says it has also changed its recommendation system to give more visibility to music made by human artists. Spotify's editors reportedly hold AI and spam tracks to the same editorial standard as other content on the platform. The announcement does not detail how Spotify identifies AI-generated tracks or what share of its catalog is affected.

stories.title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now reopen closed eyes in photos with generative AI
stories.summary: Adobe says the mobile version of Lightroom, on iOS, iPadOS and Android, can now use generative AI to open closed eyes in photos with a single tap.
stories.more: Adobe announced the feature for Lightroom mobile, available on iOS, iPadOS, and Android. When the app detects a person or group of people with their eyes closed in a photo, it automatically offers a quick action to fix it using generative AI, applied with a single tap. The announcement does not specify whether the feature works on older photos already in a library or requires a subscription tier.

stories.title: Meta Muse exposed users' personal and business secrets in shared conversations
stories.summary: Meta has suspended Muse's conversation-sharing feature after it was found to expose users' personal and business secrets when conversations were shared, while it investigates the privacy issue.
stories.more: The flaw surfaced through Muse's feature for sharing AI conversations, which reportedly could leak personal and business secrets contained in those conversations. Meta has suspended the sharing feature while it investigates. The excerpt does not specify how the exposure happened, how many users were affected, or when the feature might return.

stories.summary: IBM Research says its ALTK-Evolve system tops the τ²-bench leaderboard for customer-service agent tasks, achieved through learned memory rather than a larger frontier model.
stories.more: The post describes ALTK-Evolve climbing the τ²-bench leaderboard specifically on customer-service tasks via a learned-memory approach, without relying on a frontier model. The Source's excerpt did not include further specifics for this Edition.

stories.title: An AI agent joined a top internet researchers' listserv, sparking reply-all chaos
stories.summary: An AI agent reportedly joined a 7,500-person listserv of leading internet researchers, and its presence triggered an ongoing reply-all uproar Wired says reveals outdated assumptions about privacy.
stories.more: The listserv in question includes roughly 7,500 members considered leading internet researchers. Reaction to the agent's appearance has been strong enough that the article calls the resulting chaos 'still unfolding.' Wired frames the episode as exposing how even internet experts hold outdated notions of privacy. The excerpt does not say who added the agent, what it was built to do, or how the list's moderators responded.

stories.title: Mistral launches Voxtral 3, a real-time multilingual voice agent SDK
stories.summary: Mistral released Voxtral 3, a voice agent SDK for real-time speech in more than 50 languages, combining accurate transcription, emotional text-to-speech, and deep tool use, hosted in the EU or self-deployed.
stories.more: Voxtral 3 is Mistral's SDK for building real-time voice agents, supporting more than 50 languages. It combines accurate speech transcription with emotional text-to-speech output, aiming for less flat-sounding synthesized voices. The SDK also supports deep tool use, letting a voice agent call external functions mid-conversation. Mistral offers it either hosted in the EU or for self-deployment, giving developers a choice on data residency. The announcement does not give a release date or additional technical benchmarks.

items.title: Voxtral 3
items.excerpt: Voxtral 3: Mistral's voice agent SDK for real-time speech in 50+ languages — accurate transcription, emotional TTS, deep tool use. EU-hosted or self-deployed.

stories.title: New SpecMRL method improves compact encodings in Matryoshka Representation Learning
stories.summary: SpecMRL extends Matryoshka Representation Learning with a parameter-derived spectral basis ordered by feature importance, so that shorter prefixes read out more effectively as compact encodings.
stories.more: Matryoshka Representation Learning lets a single embedding be truncated to different lengths by jointly optimizing nested prefixes of a representation. The paper argues this approach has no explicit constraint ensuring the leading, shortest prefix actually captures a good compact encoding. SpecMRL addresses this by reorganizing the feature space around a spectral basis derived from the model's own parameters, ordered by feature importance, so the most important information lands in the earliest dimensions. This is meant to make truncated prefixes read out more reliably. The excerpt does not specify which benchmarks or datasets were used to test the method.

stories.title: MIT Technology Review on the shifting economics of enterprise AI spending
stories.summary: A Technology Review piece compares enterprise AI adoption to early electrification, arguing that as AI becomes infrastructure, the key question shifts from whether to use it to how efficiently it is used.
stories.more: The piece uses an analogy to electricity: once only a few machines ran on it, efficiency wasn't a concern, but once it became infrastructure that every process depended on, the focus shifted to efficient use. It frames enterprise AI as approaching that same infrastructure stage. The excerpt does not detail specific companies, cost figures, or efficiency metrics referenced in the full piece.

items.title: The new economics of enterprise AI
items.excerpt: Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious. But once electricity becomes infrastructure, every process depends on it, and the question changes from “can we use it?” to “how efficiently are we using it?”…

stories.title: MIT Technology Review: AI adoption lessons extend beyond Silicon Valley
stories.summary: A Technology Review piece argues the dominant narrative about AI in the workplace is too focused on Silicon Valley, and that broader cross-industry adoption trends are now reshaping software engineering and product management.
stories.more: The piece argues that treating the tech sector as an island misses how adoption trends have historically played out across other industries. It says tech is simply the first sector in line for shifts now also reaching software engineering and product management. The excerpt does not name the specific industries or adoption data the full piece draws on.

stories.title: US orders federal agencies to remove DeepSeek AI over security concerns
stories.summary: The US government has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove China's DeepSeek AI products and any third-party services built on its technology, citing national security concerns.
stories.more: The order covers DeepSeek's own products as well as third-party services that incorporate DeepSeek's underlying technology. The stated rationale is national security. The excerpt does not specify which agency issued the order, a compliance deadline, or whether private contractors are also covered.

items.title: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems
items.excerpt: The US has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products and third-party services built using its technology, citing national security concerns.

stories.title: Army Cyber Command's ECHOTRIBBLE would turn AI agents into self-spreading cyberweapons
stories.summary: Internal documents reportedly describe ECHOTRIBBLE, an Army Cyber Command program developing AI agents that spread through networks like a worm and 'neutralize' targets with minimal human oversight.
stories.more: The program is designed so its AI agents can move through other networks autonomously and reach even air-gapped systems with no network connection, according to internal documents. It is meant to operate with minimal human oversight. Experts cited in the report warn about collateral damage, noting that AI agents have recently broken into outside systems unintentionally, without any order to attack. The excerpt does not say which agency produced the documents or what stage of development the program has reached.

stories.more: Clairic is positioned specifically for document data extraction rather than general-purpose language tasks. Cloudflare's claim is that it beats LLMs on both speed and cost for this task. The excerpt does not include benchmark numbers, pricing, or details on how the model is accessed.

stories.summary: Figma co-founder Dylan Field said the Model Context Protocol isn't a perfect standard; Figma says it plans to support as many standards as possible without exposing all of its data.
stories.more: Field's comments come as Figma considers how open to be with its design data through protocols like MCP. The company says it wants to support as many standards as possible while still controlling how much of its underlying data gets exposed to external tools and agents. The excerpt does not detail which specific shortcomings Field sees in MCP or what alternative approach Figma favors.

stories.title: Robotic-arm startup Eka valued at $1.45 billion on physical AI model
stories.summary: Eka Robotics has reached a $1.45 billion valuation, driven by a physical AI model that reportedly makes its robotic arm smooth and human-like at picking up a wide range of objects.
stories.more: The valuation is tied to Eka's physical AI model, which controls a robotic arm described as unusually capable at picking up a wide variety of objects. The excerpt characterizes the motion as smooth and human-like, drawing attention from industry observers. Details on the funding round, investors, or the model's underlying architecture are not included in the excerpt available for this Edition.
